original.title: Bacon and Cabbage with Parsley Sauce
original.description: Ireland's quintessential Sunday dinner: a boiled bacon joint served with tender cabbage, floury potatoes, and a creamy parsley sauce.
ingredients: 3 lb boneless smoked pork shoulder or bacon joint (collar or loin)
1 head green cabbage, cored and cut into wedges
1/2 cup cooking liquid from the bacon
steps: Place the bacon joint in a large pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, then drain and discard the water to remove excess salt.
Return the joint to the pot with the onion, bay leaf, and peppercorns, cover with fresh cold water, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer, partly covered, for about 20 minutes per pound (roughly 1 hour), until a skewer slides easily into the meat.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20 to 25 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.
Lift the cooked bacon onto a board, cover loosely with foil, and let it rest for 15 minutes; reserve the cooking liquid.
Bring the bacon cooking liquid back to a boil, add the cabbage wedges, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until just tender.
Drain the cabbage well and toss it with 2 tablespoons butter and plenty of black pepper.
For the sauce, melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute without browning.
Gradually whisk in the milk and 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid, then simmer, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until smooth and thickened.
Stir in the parsley and pepper, taste, and add salt only if needed, since the bacon liquid is salty.
Slice the bacon thickly and serve with the cabbage, potatoes, and parsley sauce spooned over.

original.title: Irish Apple Cake
original.description: A moist, buttery cake studded with tart apples and topped with crunchy sugar, traditionally served warm with custard or cream.
ingredients: 3 tart cooking apples (such as Granny Smith), peeled, cored, and chopped
2 tbsp demerara or turbinado sugar, for topping
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease and line a 9-inch springform pan.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt together in a large bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the flour with your fingertips until the mixture looks like fine breadcrumbs, then stir in the granulated sugar.
Beat the eggs with the milk and vanilla, then stir into the dry ingredients to make a thick, soft batter.
Fold in the chopped apples until evenly distributed.
Spread the batter in the prepared pan and sprinkle the demerara sugar evenly over the top.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until golden brown and a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then release the sides and serve warm with custard, whipped cream, or vanilla ice cream.

original.title: Barmbrack
original.description: A lightly sweet, tea-soaked yeasted fruit bread traditionally baked for Halloween with a ring hidden inside to foretell a wedding.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups mixed dried fruit (raisins, sultanas, currants)
1 tsp ground mixed spice (or 1/2 tsp cinnamon plus 1/4 tsp each nutmeg and allspice)
steps: Pour the hot tea over the dried fruit and peel in a bowl, cover, and soak for at least 1 hour (or overnight), then drain well, reserving the tea.
Combine the flour, mixed spice, salt, brown sugar, and yeast in a large bowl.
Add the lukewarm milk, melted butter, beaten egg, and 2 tablespoons of the reserved tea, and mix to a soft dough.
Knead on a floured surface for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Knead in the drained fruit until evenly distributed, adding a little flour if the dough becomes sticky.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for about 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Punch down, shape into a loaf, and place in a greased 9x5-inch loaf pan; if you like, push a foil-wrapped ring into the dough.
Cover and let rise for 30 to 45 minutes until risen just above the rim of the pan, and preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Bake for 40 to 50 minutes, until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.
Dissolve the sugar in the boiling water, brush over the hot loaf, and return to the oven for 2 minutes to set the glaze.
Cool on a wire rack and serve sliced and buttered, or toasted.

original.title: Potato Farls
original.description: Northern Irish griddle potato bread made from leftover mashed potatoes, an essential part of an Ulster fry.
ingredients: 1 lb floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
2/3 cup all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
1 tbsp butter or bacon fat, for frying
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until very tender, then drain and let them steam dry for a few minutes.
Mash the potatoes until completely smooth while still warm, then stir in the melted butter and salt.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and work gently into the potato until it forms a soft dough; do not overwork it.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and pat or roll it into a round about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thick and 9 inches across.
Cut the round into quarters (farls) with a floured knife.
Heat a heavy skillet or griddle over medium heat and dry-cook the farls for 3 to 4 minutes per side until speckled brown.
To serve, fry the farls in butter or bacon fat for 2 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

original.title: Irish Seafood Chowder
original.description: A creamy, smoky chowder loaded with fish and shellfish, served all along the Irish coast with a slice of brown bread.
ingredients: 8 oz skinless salmon fillet, cut into chunks
8 oz smoked haddock or cod, cut into chunks
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the bacon for 4 minutes until it renders its fat.
Add the onion, leek, celery, and carrots and cook gently for 6 to 8 minutes until softened but not browned.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the fish stock, then add the potatoes and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the potatoes are just tender.
Add the salmon and smoked fish, then scatter the mussels on top, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes until the mussels open; discard any that stay closed.
Stir in the cream and pepper and heat through gently without boiling.
Remove the bay leaf, taste for salt, sprinkle with parsley, and serve with brown soda bread and butter.

original.title: Irish Coffee
original.description: Hot coffee spiked with Irish whiskey and brown sugar, crowned with a float of lightly whipped cream.
ingredients: 5 oz (2/3 cup) hot, strong brewed coffee
2 tbsp heavy cream, lightly whipped until just thickened
steps: Warm a stemmed glass or mug by filling it with hot water, then empty it.
Add the brown sugar and pour in the hot coffee, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the Irish whiskey.
Hold a spoon upside down just above the surface of the coffee and slowly pour the lightly whipped cream over the back of the spoon so it floats on top.
Serve immediately without stirring, drinking the coffee through the cool cream.

original.title: Irish Porridge
original.description: Creamy, slow-cooked steel-cut oatmeal with a pinch of salt, finished with brown sugar, cream, and a drizzle of honey or a splash of whiskey.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh berries or sliced banana (optional)
steps: Bring the water and milk to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Stir in the oats and salt, reduce the heat to low, and simmer, stirring often, for 25 to 30 minutes until thick and creamy.
Add a splash more water or milk if the porridge becomes too thick before the oats are tender.
Remove from the heat, cover, and let stand for 2 minutes.
Spoon into bowls and top each with brown sugar or honey, a little cream, and fruit if using.

original.title: Irish Cream Cheesecake
original.description: A rich baked cheesecake flavored with Irish cream liqueur on a chocolate cookie crust, topped with whipped cream and chocolate shavings.
steps: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C) and wrap the outside of a 9-inch springform pan with foil.
Mix the cookie crumbs with the melted butter, press firmly into the bottom of the pan, and bake for 10 minutes; let cool.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar until smooth, then beat in the flour.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating on low speed just until combined.
Mix in the Irish cream, sour cream, and vanilla until smooth, scraping the bowl well.
Pour the filling over the crust and set the pan in a roasting pan; pour hot water into the roasting pan to come halfway up the sides.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes, until the edges are set but the center still wobbles slightly.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let the cheesecake cool inside for 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar and Irish cream to soft peaks.
Spread or pipe the cream over the cheesecake and finish with grated chocolate before slicing.

original.title: Irish Shepherd's Pie
original.description: Minced lamb simmered with vegetables in a rich stout gravy and topped with buttery mashed potatoes, baked until golden.
ingredients: 2 lb floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender, drain, and mash with the butter, milk, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the lamb for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up; spoon off excess fat.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir, then add the stout, stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, remaining salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the gravy is thick, then stir in the peas.
Spread the filling in a 9x13-inch or 3-quart baking dish and spoon the mashed potatoes over, sealing to the edges.
Rough up the surface with a fork so it crisps in the oven.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling and golden on top, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

original.title: Irish Buttermilk Scones
original.description: Light, tender scones made with buttermilk, perfect split warm and spread with butter and jam.
ingredients: 3/4 cup buttermilk, plus 1 tbsp for brushing
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs, then stir in the raisins if using.
Beat the egg with the buttermilk, pour into the flour mixture, and stir with a fork just until a soft dough forms.
Turn out onto a floured surface, knead lightly 3 or 4 times, and pat to a 1-inch (2.5 cm) thickness.
Cut out rounds with a floured 2 1/2-inch cutter, pressing straight down without twisting, and place on the baking sheet.
Brush the tops with buttermilk.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden, then cool slightly and serve with butter and jam.

original.title: Full Irish Breakfast
original.description: The hearty traditional fry-up of sausages, rashers, black and white pudding, eggs, tomatoes, and mushrooms, served with soda bread.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°F (95°C) to keep cooked items warm.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and fry the sausages for 12 to 15 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through; transfer to the oven.
Fry the rashers in the same pan for 2 to 3 minutes per side and keep warm.
Fry the black and white pudding slices for 2 minutes per side until crisp at the edges and keep warm.
Season the tomatoes and cook them cut side down for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Melt half the butter in the pan and sauté the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden.
Wipe the pan, melt the remaining butter over medium-low heat, and fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Arrange everything on warm plates and serve with buttered soda bread and a pot of tea.

original.title: Dublin Lawyer
original.description: A luxurious Dublin dish of lobster meat flambéed in Irish whiskey and finished in a rich cream sauce.
steps: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil, plunge in the lobsters, and cook for 8 minutes.
Transfer the lobsters to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking, then drain.
Split the lobsters in half lengthwise, remove the meat from the tails and claws, and cut it into bite-size chunks; rinse and reserve the half shells.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the shallot for 2 minutes until soft.
Add the lobster meat and toss for 1 minute to warm through.
Pour in the whiskey and carefully ignite it with a long match, letting the flames die down.
Stir in the cream, mustard, lemon juice, salt, and cayenne and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Spoon the lobster and sauce back into the warmed shells, sprinkle with parsley, and serve at once.

original.title: Smoked Salmon on Brown Bread
original.description: A classic Irish starter of silky smoked salmon on buttered brown soda bread with lemon, capers, and red onion.
ingredients: 1/4 small red onion, very thinly sliced
2 tbsp crème fraîche or sour cream (optional)
steps: Spread each slice of brown bread generously with butter.
Drape the smoked salmon in loose folds over the bread.
Top with a few slices of red onion and a scattering of capers.
Add a small dollop of crème fraîche if using.
Sprinkle with dill and freshly ground black pepper.
Cut each slice in half and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing over.

original.title: Mussels in Cider and Cream
original.description: Plump Irish mussels steamed in dry cider with garlic and shallots, finished with cream and parsley.
steps: Discard any mussels with cracked shells or that do not close when tapped.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the shallots and garlic for 2 to 3 minutes until soft.
Pour in the cider, raise the heat to high, and bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, cover tightly, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pot once or twice, until the shells open.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the mussels to warm bowls, discarding any that remain closed.
Stir the cream and pepper into the cooking liquid and boil for 1 minute.
Pour the sauce over the mussels, sprinkle with parsley, and serve with crusty bread or brown bread.

original.title: Steak and Guinness Pie
original.description: Tender chunks of beef braised in Guinness with onions and mushrooms under a golden puff pastry lid, a favorite of Irish pubs.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 1/2 cups Guinness or other Irish stout
steps: Toss the beef with the flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, 4 to 5 minutes per batch; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, onions, and mushrooms and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until browned, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the stout, scraping up the browned bits, then add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar, thyme, and the beef.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 2 hours until the beef is very tender and the gravy has thickened.
Remove the thyme stems and let the filling cool for at least 20 minutes so it does not melt the pastry.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and spoon the filling into a 2-quart pie dish.
Lay the puff pastry over the dish, trim and crimp the edges, cut a small steam vent, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

original.title: Homemade Irish Cream Liqueur
original.description: A smooth, creamy whiskey liqueur made at home in minutes, lovely in coffee or over ice and a popular Christmas gift.
steps: Pour all the ingredients into a blender.
Blend on low speed for 30 seconds until completely smooth; do not overblend or the cream may thicken.
Pour into clean glass bottles and seal tightly.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving to let the flavors meld.
Shake well before pouring and serve over ice or in coffee; keep refrigerated and use within 2 months.

original.title: Hot Whiskey
original.description: Ireland's cure-all: Irish whiskey with hot water, lemon, cloves, and brown sugar, sipped on cold nights.
steps: Warm a heatproof glass by filling it with hot water, then empty it.
Stud the lemon slice with the cloves.
Add the brown sugar and whiskey to the glass.
Pour in the boiling water and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Drop in the clove-studded lemon slice and serve hot.

original.title: Guinness Chocolate Cake
original.description: A dark, moist chocolate cake made with Irish stout and topped with a tangy cream cheese frosting that looks like the head on a pint.
ingredients: 1 cup Guinness or other Irish stout
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease and line a 9-inch springform pan.
Heat the stout and butter in a saucepan until the butter melts, then whisk in the cocoa and sugar until smooth; remove from the heat.
Beat the sour cream, eggs, and vanilla together and whisk into the chocolate mixture.
Whisk in the flour and baking soda until the batter is smooth.
Pour into the prepared pan and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack, then remove.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth, then beat in the powdered sugar.
Add the heavy cream and beat until thick and spreadable.
Spread the frosting over the top of the cake so it resembles the creamy head of a pint, and slice to serve.

original.title: Irish Porter Cake
original.description: A dense, moist fruit cake made with stout and spice, a traditional Irish teatime and Christmas cake that keeps for weeks.
ingredients: 3 cups mixed dried fruit (raisins, sultanas, currants)
2 tsp ground mixed spice (or 1 tsp cinnamon plus 1/2 tsp each nutmeg and allspice)
steps: Place the butter, brown sugar, and stout in a large saucepan and heat gently until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves.
Add the dried fruit, mixed peel, and orange zest, bring to a boil, and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from the heat and let cool until just warm, about 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease and line an 8-inch round deep cake pan with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, and mixed spice together.
Stir the beaten eggs into the cooled fruit mixture, then fold in the flour mixture until no dry streaks remain.
Spoon the batter into the pan and level the top.
Bake for 1 1/2 to 1 3/4 hours, covering loosely with foil if browning too quickly, until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool completely in the pan, then wrap well; the flavor improves after a day or two.

original.title: Carrageen Moss Pudding
original.description: A delicate, old-fashioned Irish milk pudding set with carrageen seaweed and flavored with lemon and vanilla.
ingredients: 1/4 oz (about 1/2 cup loosely packed) dried carrageen moss
steps: Soak the carrageen in lukewarm water for 10 minutes, then drain and pick out any grit.
Place the carrageen, milk, and lemon zest in a saucepan and bring slowly to a simmer.
Simmer very gently for 20 minutes, until the moss swells and the milk thickens slightly.
Beat the egg yolk with the sugar and vanilla in a bowl.
Strain the hot milk onto the yolk mixture through a sieve, pushing through all the jelly from the carrageen, and whisk well.
Beat the egg white to stiff peaks and gently fold it into the mixture.
Pour into a serving bowl or individual glasses and chill for 2 to 3 hours until set.
Serve with poached fruit, berries, or a drizzle of cream.

original.title: Irish Rhubarb Tart
original.description: A homely shortcrust pastry tart filled with sweet-tart rhubarb, a springtime favorite in Irish kitchens.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb rhubarb, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, and salt, then rub in the butter until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Add the egg yolk and enough ice water to bring the dough together, divide in two, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and place a baking sheet in the oven to heat.
Toss the rhubarb with the sugar and cornstarch.
Roll out one piece of pastry and line a 9-inch pie plate, then fill with the rhubarb mixture.
Roll out the second piece, lay it over the filling, trim, and crimp the edges to seal.
Brush the top with beaten egg, sprinkle with sugar, and cut a few steam vents.
Bake on the hot baking sheet for 40 to 45 minutes until the pastry is golden and the juices bubble through the vents.
Cool for at least 30 minutes and serve warm with custard or softly whipped cream.

original.title: Apple and Blackberry Crumble
original.description: Late-summer apples and wild blackberries baked under a buttery oat crumble, served with custard or cream.
ingredients: 2 lb cooking apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Toss the apples and blackberries with the sugar and lemon juice and spread them in a 2-quart baking dish.
Mix the flour, oats, brown sugar, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture forms coarse clumps.
Scatter the crumble evenly over the fruit without pressing it down.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the topping is golden and the fruit juices bubble up at the edges.
Let stand for 10 minutes and serve warm with custard, cream, or vanilla ice cream.

original.title: Bread and Butter Pudding
original.description: Slices of buttered bread layered with raisins and baked in a vanilla-scented custard until puffed and golden.
steps: Grease a 2-quart baking dish with butter.
Butter the bread on one side, cut each slice into triangles, and arrange half of them, buttered side up, in the dish.
Scatter half the raisins over, then add the remaining bread and raisins.
Whisk the eggs and sugar together, then whisk in the milk, cream, and vanilla.
Pour the custard evenly over the bread and let it soak for 20 minutes, pressing the bread down gently.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Sprinkle the top with nutmeg and demerara sugar.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the custard is just set and the top is crisp and golden.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving warm.

original.title: Dingle Pies
original.description: Traditional Kerry hand pies of spiced minced mutton or lamb in hot-water pastry, once made for fair days and Lammas.
ingredients: 1 lb lamb shoulder, finely diced or coarsely ground
steps: Mix the lamb, onion, carrot, cumin, salt, pepper, and parsley in a bowl and set aside.
For the pastry, mix the flour and salt in a large bowl and make a well in the center.
Heat the water, lard, and butter in a saucepan until the fat melts and the mixture boils.
Pour the hot liquid into the flour and stir quickly to form a dough, then knead briefly until smooth while still warm.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Roll out two-thirds of the pastry and cut six 6-inch rounds; roll the remaining pastry and cut six 4-inch rounds for lids.
Spoon the filling onto the large rounds, moisten each with a spoonful of stock, then gather up the edges and top with the lids, pinching firmly to seal.
Cut a small hole in each lid and brush the pies with beaten egg.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until deep golden, pouring a little hot stock through the holes halfway through if the filling looks dry.
Serve hot or cold.

original.title: Roast Leg of Lamb with Mint Sauce
original.description: A garlic and rosemary-studded leg of lamb roasted until pink and served with a sharp, fresh mint sauce, the traditional Irish Easter dinner.
ingredients: 1 bone-in leg of lamb (5 to 6 lb)
3 sprigs fresh rosemary, broken into small sprigs
1 cup packed fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
1/4 cup white wine vinegar or malt vinegar
steps: Take the lamb out of the refrigerator 1 hour before cooking and preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Make small, deep cuts all over the lamb with a sharp knife and push a sliver of garlic and a small sprig of rosemary into each one.
Rub the lamb with olive oil, salt, and pepper and place it in a roasting pan.
Roast for 20 minutes, then reduce the heat to 350°F (175°C) and roast for about 15 minutes per pound for medium-rare, until an instant-read thermometer reads 135°F (57°C) in the thickest part.
Meanwhile, make the mint sauce: stir the sugar into the boiling water until dissolved, add the chopped mint and vinegar, and let stand for at least 30 minutes.
Transfer the lamb to a board, cover loosely with foil, and rest for 20 minutes.
Spoon off the fat from the roasting pan, add the stock, and boil on the stovetop for 3 to 4 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, to make a thin gravy.
Carve the lamb and serve with the pan juices, mint sauce, and roast potatoes.

original.title: Irish Fish Pie
original.description: Chunks of salmon, white fish, and smoked haddock in a creamy parsley sauce, topped with mashed potatoes and baked until golden.
ingredients: 2 lb floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
12 oz skinless cod or haddock fillet
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender, drain, and mash with 2 tablespoons butter and 1/4 cup milk.
Place the 2 1/2 cups milk, bay leaf, and onion in a wide pan, add all the fish, and poach gently for 6 to 8 minutes until just cooked.
Lift out the fish, flake it into large chunks, and place in a 2 1/2-quart baking dish; strain and reserve the milk.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Melt 3 tablespoons butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the reserved poaching milk and simmer, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until thick and smooth.
Stir in the parsley, lemon juice, salt, and pepper, then pour the sauce over the fish and tuck in the egg quarters.
Spread the mashed potatoes over the top, fork the surface, dot with the remaining butter, and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling and golden brown, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

original.title: Chicken and Leek Pie
original.description: A comforting pub-style pie of tender chicken and soft leeks in a creamy tarragon sauce beneath a flaky pastry crust.
ingredients: 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
3 leeks, white and light green parts, sliced and washed
1 tbsp chopped fresh tarragon or 1 tsp dried
steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in batches for 4 to 5 minutes; set aside.
Add the bacon and leeks to the pan and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until the leeks are soft.
Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the stock and cream, then add the mustard, tarragon, salt, pepper, and chicken.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken is cooked through, then let cool for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and spoon the filling into a 2-quart pie dish.
Cover with the puff pastry, trim and crimp the edges, cut a steam vent, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

original.title: Irish Vegetable Soup
original.description: The smooth, thick blended vegetable soup served in every Irish pub and home kitchen, best with a wedge of brown bread.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low heat.
Add the onion, leek, carrots, celery, and parsnip, cover, and sweat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened but not browned.
Add the potatoes, stock, salt, and pepper and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes until all the vegetables are very tender.
Purée the soup with an immersion blender or in batches in a blender until smooth.
Stir in the milk or cream and reheat gently without boiling.
Taste for seasoning, sprinkle with parsley, and serve with brown soda bread.

original.title: Irish Nettle Soup
original.description: A bright green spring tonic made from young nettle tops, potatoes, and onion, traditionally eaten in Ireland in early spring.
ingredients: 8 cups (about 6 oz) young nettle tops, picked with gloves
steps: Wearing gloves, wash the nettle tops well and discard any tough stalks.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low heat and cook the onion and leek for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes, stock, salt, and pepper, bring to a boil, and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the nettles and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until they wilt and turn deep green.
Purée the soup until smooth with an immersion blender or in a blender.
Stir in the cream, reheat gently, and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with a swirl of cream and brown bread.

original.title: Warm Black Pudding and Apple Salad
original.description: Crisp slices of Irish black pudding and caramelized apple over peppery greens with a mustard-cider dressing.
ingredients: 8 oz black pudding, cut into 1/2-inch slices
2 crisp apples, cored and cut into wedges
5 oz mixed salad leaves or watercress
steps: Whisk the dressing ingredients together in a small bowl.
Melt half the butter in a skillet over medium-high heat, add the apple wedges, sprinkle with sugar, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden; remove.
Add the remaining butter to the pan and fry the black pudding slices for 2 minutes per side until crisp at the edges.
Toss the salad leaves with most of the dressing and divide among plates.
Top with the warm apple and black pudding, drizzle with the remaining dressing, and serve immediately.

original.title: Spice Bag
original.description: Dublin's favorite takeaway: crispy chicken strips, chips, peppers, and onions tossed in a spicy salt-and-pepper seasoning.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into strips
steps: Mix all the spice mix ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.
Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat the frying oil in a deep pot to 325°F (160°C) and fry the potatoes in batches for 5 minutes until soft but pale; drain on paper towels.
Dip the chicken strips in beaten egg, then toss in the mixed cornstarch and flour, shaking off the excess.
Raise the oil temperature to 350°F (175°C) and fry the chicken in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through; drain.
Increase the oil to 375°F (190°C) and fry the potatoes again for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and golden; drain.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat and stir-fry the bell pepper, onion, and chili for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken, fries, and scallions to the wok, sprinkle with 2 to 3 teaspoons of the spice mix, and toss well to coat.
Serve at once in paper bags or bowls, with curry sauce on the side if you like.

original.title: Yellowman
original.description: A crunchy golden honeycomb toffee from Northern Ireland, famously sold at the Ould Lammas Fair in Ballycastle.
ingredients: 1/2 cup golden syrup or light corn syrup
steps: Grease an 8-inch square pan with butter.
Combine the sugar, syrup, butter, vinegar, and water in a large heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Raise the heat and boil without stirring until the mixture reaches 300°F (150°C) on a candy thermometer, the hard-crack stage, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove from the heat and immediately whisk in the baking soda; the mixture will foam up dramatically.
Pour at once into the prepared pan without spreading it, so the bubbles stay intact.
Let cool completely for about 1 hour until hard.
Break into pieces and store in an airtight container.

original.title: Glazed Baked Ham
original.description: A clove-studded ham glazed with brown sugar, mustard, and whiskey, the centerpiece of an Irish Christmas table.
ingredients: 1 fully cooked bone-in half ham (7 to 8 lb)
steps: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
Remove any skin from the ham, leaving a thin layer of fat, and score the fat in a 1-inch diamond pattern.
Stud the center of each diamond with a whole clove.
Place the ham in a roasting pan, pour the water into the pan, and cover loosely with foil.
Bake for about 15 minutes per pound (1 3/4 to 2 hours), until it reaches 130°F (55°C) inside.
Stir the glaze ingredients together in a small saucepan and simmer for 2 minutes until syrupy.
Remove the foil, raise the oven to 400°F (200°C), and brush the ham generously with the glaze.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes more, brushing with glaze twice, until the surface is sticky and caramelized.
Rest for 15 minutes before carving and serve hot or cold.

original.title: Irish Sausage Rolls
original.description: Seasoned pork sausage meat wrapped in flaky puff pastry, a staple of Irish parties, picnics, and deli counters.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Mix the sausage meat, onion, breadcrumbs, parsley, thyme, and pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Cut each pastry sheet in half lengthwise to make four long strips.
Divide the sausage mixture into four and roll each into a log the length of the pastry, then lay it along one long edge of each strip.
Brush the far edge of the pastry with beaten egg, roll the pastry over the filling, and press to seal with the seam underneath.
Cut each log into 6 pieces, place on the baking sheets, and cut two small slashes in the top of each.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds if using.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until puffed, golden, and cooked through, then serve warm or at room temperature.

original.title: Irish Pancakes with Lemon and Sugar
original.description: Thin, crêpe-like pancakes sprinkled with sugar and lemon juice, the beloved Irish way to celebrate Shrove Tuesday.
ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
steps: Sift the flour and salt into a bowl and make a well in the center.
Crack in the eggs, add a little of the milk, and whisk, gradually drawing in the flour.
Whisk in the remaining milk and the melted butter to make a smooth batter the consistency of light cream, then rest it for 15 minutes.
Heat an 8-inch skillet over medium-high heat and brush lightly with butter.
Pour in about 3 tablespoons of batter and swirl to coat the base thinly.
Cook for about 1 minute until the underside is golden, then flip and cook for 30 seconds more.
Slide onto a warm plate, sprinkle with sugar, squeeze over lemon juice, and roll up or fold into quarters.
Repeat with the remaining batter, serving each pancake as it is made.
